title: Rethinking Fair Graph Neural Networks from Re-balancing

problem.claim: Distribution disparities between demographic groups create fairness concerns in high-stakes GNN-based decision-making systems.

gap.claim: Existing fair GNN methods require substantial architectural changes or additional loss functions with more hyper-parameter tuning.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes FairGB, a fair GNN approach based on group re-balancing.
FairGB combines counterfactual node mixup with contribution alignment loss.
The authors provide a causal-view analysis and claim that the strategy can make sensitive attributes statistically independent from target labels.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Simple re-balancing methods can match or surpass existing fair GNN methods.
Experiments on benchmark datasets report state-of-the-art utility and fairness metrics.
Code is reported as available in the linked repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are widely deployed because of their strong representation ability.
Demographic distribution disparities raise fairness concerns in high-stakes decision-making.
Recent fair GNN methods often require architectural changes or additional hyper-parameter tuning.
The authors attribute unfairness to demographic imbalance and imbalanced group contributions to parameter updates, while noting shortcomings during training for simple re-balancing methods.
FairGB combines counterfactual node mixup and gradient-based contribution alignment, with reported causal analysis and benchmark results for utility and fairness.

source_observation.claim: Demographic imbalance can produce imbalanced contributions to parameter updates.

interpretation.claim: Training-data or group-contribution imbalance may be a direct mechanism contributing to unfair model behavior.

application.claim: When auditing fairness, examine group balance and group-specific optimization contributions before introducing architectural changes.

exception.claim: Simple re-balancing methods may have shortcomings during training.

source_observation.claim: FairGB combines counterfactual sample generation with gradient-based contribution reweighting.

interpretation.claim: Fairness interventions can combine data-level balancing with optimization-level alignment.

application.claim: A fairness method may pair counterfactual augmentation with group-aware gradient contribution adjustment.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which datasets, metrics, or training conditions support the reported results.

unknowns: Benchmark dataset identities and sizes are unspecified.
Utility and fairness metric values are unspecified.
The scope and formal assumptions of the causal analysis are unspecified.
Training shortcomings of simple re-balancing methods are not described in detail.
